# Punctuation and formatting

Dashes, quotes, markup, headings, lists and emoji.

Tags: strength (`hard` always · `default` unless an exception or the sensitivity says otherwise · `soft` preference) · kind (`ai-tell`, `clarity`, `both`, `procedure`).

### FMT-001 · bold overuse
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Use bold rarely, for the one term or warning a reader must not miss; do not bold key phrases, proper nouns or every instance of a term.

- Threshold: **standard:** at most one bolded phrase per section (or per ~300 words); never the same term twice · **strict:** no bold in running prose except UI element names in docs and safety warnings · **relaxed:** flag only when bold appears in most paragraphs or on random words
- Triggers: `**`
- Exceptions: UI element names in procedures; defined terms on first use in reference docs; warnings and admonitions; chat or posts where the voice corpus uses bold
- Example: ✗ **Kubernetes** gives you **scalability** and **resilience**. → ✓ Kubernetes restarts failed pods automatically.

### FMT-002 · inline-header (bold label + colon) list
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not build lists where each item opens with a bold label and a colon; write prose, or plain items, unless the label names a distinct term and the text adds new detail.

- Threshold: **standard:** lists where every item has a bold label + colon, or where a label restates its line · **strict:** any bold-label-colon list in prose or chat · **relaxed:** only labels that restate their line
- Exceptions: reference docs, glossaries, API parameter lists, changelogs and option tables (criterion 5); a bold lead-in that names the item and is followed by new detail
- Example: ✗ - **Performance:** Performance is better. / - **Security:** Security is improved. → ✓ Queries run in 40 ms instead of 300 ms, and tokens now expire after an hour.

### FMT-003 · bullet overuse
`default · both · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not fragment reasoning into bullets; keep lists for content that is truly list-shaped, and remove redundant or verbless noun-phrase bullets.

- Threshold: **standard:** bullet-heavy sections that are not list-shaped; 5+ verbless adjective+noun bullets; duplicate items · **strict:** any list whose items depend on each other (because, so, but) becomes prose · **relaxed:** only duplicate or redundant bullets
- Exceptions: steps, requirements, feature comparisons, API parameters, checklists, enumerations; docs and READMEs where scanning is the main use (criterion 5)
- Example: ✗ - Fast performance / - Robust security / - Seamless integration / - Modern design / - Great support → ✓ It builds in under a minute and signs every artefact. It has no plugin system yet.

### FMT-004 · list construction
`default · clarity · scope: prose · voice can override`

When a list is warranted, number sequences, bullet everything else, introduce the list with a full sentence and keep items grammatically parallel.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: a lead-in that only announces the list ('The reasons are as follows:') is rewritten into a sentence with content, or dropped when the previous sentence already introduces the list; never remove list items
- Example: ✗ Steps: / - Installing / - You configure it / - Run → ✓ To set up the agent: / 1. Install it. / 2. Configure it. / 3. Run it.

### FMT-005 · pseudo-document structure in short replies
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not dress short replies, chat messages or DMs as documents with headers, numbered bold sections or heavy lists; documents keep their structure.

- Threshold: **standard:** no headers in replies under ~300 words; at most one numbered bold subsection per reply · **strict:** no headers, bold or lists in replies under ~300 words · **relaxed:** flag only when headers outnumber paragraphs
- Exceptions: documents, READMEs, reports (criterion 5); user or corpus that uses such formatting in chat; user asked for a list
- Example: ✗ ## Summary / **1. The fix** / ... / **2. Next steps** → ✓ The fix is in main. Next, rerun the nightly job.

### FMT-006 · title case headings
`default · both · scope: prose · voice can override`

Write headings in sentence case (capitalise the first word and proper nouns) unless the destination's house style says otherwise.

- Threshold: **standard:** sentence case for subheadings; main title follows house style · **strict:** sentence case for every heading including the title · **relaxed:** flag only when it clashes with the rest of the document
- Exceptions: house style or existing document convention with title case (criterion 6); proper nouns and product names
- Example: ✗ ## Key Benefits Of The New Pipeline → ✓ ## Benefits of the new pipeline

### FMT-007 · headings label content
`default · clarity · scope: prose · voice can override`

Make each heading name what its section holds: a verb phrase for tasks, a noun phrase for concepts, never a teaser written for effect.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: creative or editorial pieces where the voice uses playful headings
- Example: ✗ ## The Secret Sauce → ✓ ## How the scheduler batches jobs

### FMT-008 · boilerplate paired headings
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not add boilerplate outline headings (Challenges and future directions, Awards and recognition, Legacy) unless the content truly is that.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `awards and recognition`, `challenges and future directions`, `challenges and legacy`, `future directions`, `recognition`
- Exceptions: sections whose content genuinely lists awards, challenges or plans
- Example: ✗ ## Challenges and Future Directions → ✓ (cut the section, or name the concrete issue: ## Open bugs in the parser)

### FMT-009 · heading hierarchy
`soft · both · scope: prose · voice can override`

Keep heading hierarchy clean: one top-level heading, no skipped levels, and no heading whose only content is more headings.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: platforms that render the page title as h1 outside the content
- Example: ✗ # Guide / ### Install / ## Usage / ### Basics → ✓ # Guide / ## Install / ... / ## Usage / Text first. / ### Basics

### FMT-010 · duplicated title heading
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not open with a heading that repeats the document title.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: formats where the title is not shown separately (plain Markdown files)
- Example: ✗ (title: Release notes) # Release notes → ✓ Start with the first section.

### FMT-011 · rules between sections
`soft · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not put a horizontal rule between every section; headings already separate them.

- Threshold: **standard:** flag rules between most sections · **strict:** no horizontal rules in prose · **relaxed:** flag only rules between every section
- Triggers: `***`, `---`
- Exceptions: slide separators, YAML front matter, one deliberate break before an appendix
- Example: ✗ ## A / text / --- / ## B / text / --- → ✓ ## A / text / ## B / text

### FMT-012 · decorative emoji
`hard · ai-tell · scope: all · voice can override`

Do not decorate headings, bullets, comments or commit messages with emoji.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: social posts: one or two at line end when the voice or platform uses them; voice corpus or repo convention that uses emoji (e.g. gitmoji repos, criterion 6); emoji as subject matter, quoted UI or user content
- Example: ✗ ## 🚀 Getting started / - ✅ Fast → ✓ ## Getting started / - Builds in under a minute

### FMT-013 · arrow chains
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Keep arrow chains (X -> Y -> Z) to three nodes; write longer flows as sentences or a numbered list.

- Threshold: **standard:** max three nodes · **strict:** no arrow chains in prose · **relaxed:** max five nodes
- Triggers: `->`, `=>`, `→`
- Exceptions: state machines, transition tables, pipelines and diagrams; code
- Example: ✗ Idea -> prototype -> feedback -> iteration -> launch -> scale → ✓ We prototype, collect feedback, then launch.

### FMT-014 · fake-structure tables
`soft · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not turn a handful of facts into a small table or use tables to simulate structure; keep tables for data with at least two real dimensions.

- Threshold: **standard:** small tables a sentence would carry · **strict:** tables with fewer than 3 rows or 2 data columns · **relaxed:** only single-column or 2-row tables
- Exceptions: reference docs and comparisons across several attributes
- Example: ✗ | Feature | Value | / | Speed | Fast | → ✓ It is fast.

### FMT-015 · code fences for payloads only
`default · clarity · scope: all · voice can override`

Reserve code fences for literal payloads: code, commands, fixtures, and copy-paste-ready text whose line breaks must survive; never fence ordinary prose for decoration.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `````
- Exceptions: drafts handed to the user for copy-paste into a platform where whitespace matters
- Example: ✗ ``` / Note: remember to restart. / ``` → ✓ Restart the service after editing the config.

### FMT-016 · markup leakage
`default · both · scope: all · voice cannot override`

Use the markup of the destination; do not leave Markdown asterisks, hash headings, fences or link syntax in plain text, email or other media that will not render them.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `##`, `**`, `[text](url)`, `````
- Exceptions: destinations that render Markdown
- Example: ✗ **Update:** see [the doc](https://x) → ✓ Update: see the design doc at https://x

### FMT-018 · hashtag stuffing
`soft · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Keep hashtags to two or three specific ones at most; do not append blocks of broad tags.

- Threshold: **standard:** flag 4 or more, or any broad tag (#AI #Innovation) · **strict:** no hashtags unless the platform needs them · **relaxed:** flag 6 or more
- Exceptions: issue refs (#123), hex colours, code, headings
- Example: ✗ #AI #Innovation #Future #Tech #Growth #Leadership → ✓ #rustlang

### FMT-019 · descriptive link text
`default · clarity · scope: prose · voice cannot override`

Make link text say where the link goes (the page title or a short description), never 'click here'.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `click here`, `here`, `this link`
- Example: ✗ Click [here](/install) to install. → ✓ See the [installation guide](/install).

### FMT-020 · docs markup conventions
`default · clarity · scope: prose · voice can override`

In technical docs put code identifiers in code font, UI element names in bold, and say up front that a list is partial instead of ending it with 'etc.'.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `etc.`
- Exceptions: house style that differs
- Example: ✗ Set timeout, retries, etc. in the Settings tab. → ✓ Set options such as `timeout` and `retries` on the **Settings** tab.

### PUN-001 · em dash rate
`hard · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not use em dashes (—); where a dash between clauses is genuinely the best mark, use a simple spaced hyphen ( - ) instead, and never as a dramatic pivot or default joint.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: ` – `, `--`, `—`
- Exceptions: en dashes in numeric or date ranges (10–20, 2019–2024) never count; dashes inside code, inline code, commands, paths, URLs and quoted material; list items that open with a bold term or link followed by a dash (definition-list style); a voice profile built from the author's own corpus whose measured habits include em dashes: when writing in that author's voice only, match the corpus's measured rate; a pasted sample or any other output follows the ban; a lone dash is not evidence of AI authorship; never cite one dash as a tell
- Example: ✗ The fix was simple — we removed the cache. → ✓ The fix was simple: we removed the cache. / The fix was simple. We removed the cache.

### PUN-002 · dash stand-ins between clauses
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Count every dash used between clauses (spaced hyphen, en dash) against one budget, and never use double hyphens (--) as a dash.

- Threshold: **standard:** at most 2 per 1,000 words and at most 1 per paragraph; none used for a reveal, pivot or punch-line · **strict:** no dashes between clauses · **relaxed:** flag only clusters: 5+ per piece or more than 4 per 1,000 words
- Triggers: ` - `, ` -- `, `–`
- Exceptions: en dash between numbers, dates, times, scores or paired names (pages 4–9, 9:00–17:00, London–Paris); hyphenated words and compound modifiers; code, CLI flags, paths, URLs, Markdown list markers
- Example: ✗ The cache was cold - so every request hit the database. → ✓ The cache was cold, so every request hit the database.

### PUN-003 · punctuation rules skip literal text
`hard · procedure · scope: all · voice cannot override`

Never edit dashes, hyphens or quotes inside code, inline code, commands, paths, URLs, numeric ranges or quoted material when applying punctuation rules.

- Exceptions: clock times, ratios, URL schemes, table delimiter rows, entity syntax and code are never violations of a punctuation ban
- Example: ✗ Changing `git log --oneline` to `git log, oneline` while removing dashes. → ✓ Leave `git log --oneline` untouched.

### PUN-004 · dash substitute becomes the new tic
`default · ai-tell · scope: all · voice can override`

When removing a dash, do not move the same habit into parentheses, colons or semicolons; prefer a period, a comma with a conjunction, or a rewrite, and keep the substitutes varied.

- Threshold: **standard:** replacements for removed dashes may not all be the same mark; parentheses and colons together stay under 2 per paragraph · **strict:** no parenthetical or colon used as a dash replacement · **relaxed:** flag only when one substitute mark repeats in most sentences of a paragraph
- Exceptions: parentheses that hold a true aside, unit, abbreviation or reference
- Example: ✗ The fix (and it is a big one) ships today (finally). → ✓ The fix ships today. It is a large change.

### PUN-005 · parenthetical hedging and fragments
`soft · both · scope: prose · voice can override`

Make a parenthetical a complete grammatical unit or move it to its own sentence; do not use parentheses to slip in hedges or second thoughts, and do not write plurals as '(s)'.

- Threshold: **standard:** parenthetical hedges such as '(and, increasingly, Z)'; any '(s)' · **strict:** any hedge or afterthought in parentheses · **relaxed:** only '(s)' plurals
- Triggers: `(s)`
- Exceptions: abbreviations, units, citations and short glosses in parentheses
- Example: ✗ Select the file(s) (and possibly the folder) to sync. → ✓ Select one or more files to sync. You can also select a folder.

### PUN-007 · colon as connector
`default · ai-tell · scope: all · voice can override`

Use a colon to introduce a list, example, quote or definition, not as a mid-sentence reveal or connector.

- Threshold: **standard:** colon reveals ('Here is the thing:', 'The result:') and more than one connector colon per paragraph · **strict:** every mid-sentence colon not introducing a list, example, quote or definition · **relaxed:** only repeated colon reveals
- Exceptions: labels in UI text, times, ratios, key: value syntax, code; ordinary colons in speech, headings, list items, a general-then-specific explanation, URLs and code never count; a signpost label before a colon (In short:, The key is:, Bottom line:) goes when the label carries no information; write the content directly; when the clause before the colon links back to earlier text, keep it and change only the colon, to a period when both sides are full clauses (never a comma splice, PUN-017); a colon introducing a list, or a short label in updates, briefs, status notes and PR descriptions, is fine; flag a colon that glues two unrelated clauses in essay-like prose
- Example: ✗ The reason is simple: the cache was cold. → ✓ The cache was cold.

### PUN-008 · semicolon use
`soft · clarity · scope: prose · voice can override`

Prefer two sentences to a semicolon in procedures and technical documentation; elsewhere semicolons are fine and are not an AI tell.

- Threshold: **standard:** semicolons allowed; count toward PUN-004 when they replace dashes · **strict:** no semicolons in procedures or reference docs, and none anywhere in strict controlled-English mode · **relaxed:** no constraint
- Triggers: `;`
- Exceptions: writer sample or voice profile that uses semicolons; code
- Example: ✗ Run the migration; then restart the API. → ✓ Run the migration. Then restart the API.

### PUN-009 · serial comma
`soft · clarity · scope: all · voice can override`

Use the serial comma by default and keep comma style consistent; follow the destination's house style or the writer's sample when it differs.

- Exceptions: house style without serial comma (many news and British styles); voice profile
- Example: ✗ We tested Postgres, MySQL and SQLite, Redis and Memcached. → ✓ We tested Postgres, MySQL, and SQLite, then Redis and Memcached.

### PUN-010 · unicode decoration
`soft · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

In plain prose typed for screens, prefer keyboard characters over hard-to-type Unicode arrows, ellipsis characters and decorative glyphs.

- Threshold: **standard:** decorative glyphs always; arrows or ellipsis characters when the rest of the text is plain ASCII · **strict:** any →, …, ✦, ★ or similar glyph in prose · **relaxed:** decorative glyphs (✦, ★, ➤) only
- Triggers: `…`, `→`, `⇒`, `★`, `✦`, `➤`
- Exceptions: typeset publishing or house styles that use typographic characters; math, UI strings and quoted material; voice profile that uses them
- Example: ✗ Input → validation → storage… → ✓ Input goes through validation, then storage.

### PUN-011 · quote style consistency
`soft · both · scope: all · voice can override`

Choose straight or curly quotes by the destination format and use one style throughout; in code-adjacent text use straight quotes. Do not treat curly quotes alone as an AI tell.

- Threshold: **standard:** match destination; flag only mixed styles in one text or curly quotes in code-adjacent text · **strict:** straight quotes everywhere unless the destination requires curly · **relaxed:** flag only mixed styles
- Triggers: `‘`, `’`, `“`, `”`
- Exceptions: locale-correct quotation marks (« », „ “); quoted material; word processors and print styles that curl quotes; curly versus straight quotes is a house or destination convention, not a tell: normalise only when the config or destination requires it, keep one style per document, and never cite quote shape as evidence of AI authorship
- Example: ✗ He said “ship it” and then "wait". → ✓ He said "ship it" and then "wait".

### PUN-012 · no injected imperfection
`hard · procedure · scope: all · voice cannot override`

Never add typos, sloppy typography or deliberate errors to make text look human; clean typography is a style choice, not a tell.

- Example: ✗ Introducing 'teh' or a missing apostrophe to look less polished. → ✓ Leave correct text correct.

### PUN-013 · typographic shouting
`default · ai-tell · scope: prose · voice can override`

Do not shout words in all caps or split them with periods for emphasis; let sentence structure carry the stress.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: acronyms, constants, UI labels, legal notices that require caps, quoted text; voice profile that does this
- Example: ✗ This is NOT optional. Every. Single. Time. → ✓ This step is required on every deploy.

### PUN-014 · hyphenated compounds after the noun
`soft · clarity · scope: prose · voice can override`

Hyphenate compound modifiers before a noun but not after it, unless the dictionary always hyphenates the word.

- Threshold: **standard:** 3 or more in a text · **strict:** every post-noun hyphenated compound · **relaxed:** n/a (do not flag)
- Triggers: `client-facing`, `high-quality`, `long-term`, `real-time`, `well-documented`, `well-known`
- Exceptions: permanently hyphenated words (third-party, cross-functional); house style
- Example: ✗ The report is high-quality and the data is real-time. → ✓ The report is high quality and the data is real time.

### PUN-015 · ambiguous slash
`default · clarity · scope: prose · voice can override`

Replace slashes that hide a logical relation ('and/or', 'a/b') with words.

- Threshold: **standard:** and/or and ad-hoc a/b pairs · **strict:** every slash in running prose outside the exceptions · **relaxed:** and/or only
- Triggers: `/`, `and/or`
- Exceptions: paths, URLs, units (km/h), fractions, dates; established terms (I/O, TCP/IP, client/server); code
- Example: ✗ Users and/or admins can edit the config/settings. → ✓ Users, admins, or both can edit the settings.

### PUN-016 · list-label punctuation
`soft · clarity · scope: prose · voice can override`

In label-led list items, punctuate consistently: a short label takes a colon and a lowercase gloss, a full-sentence lead-in takes a period.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: destination style guide
- Example: ✗ - Speed. faster builds → ✓ - Speed: builds finish in half the time

### PUN-017 · comma splice
`default · clarity · scope: all · voice can override`

Do not join two independent clauses with only a comma; use a period, a conjunction or a semicolon.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: very short parallel clauses used deliberately in a writer's voice; quoted material
- Example: ✗ The tests passed, the build failed. → ✓ The tests passed, but the build failed.

### PUN-018 · complete comma pairs
`soft · clarity · scope: prose · voice can override`

Close a parenthetic aside with the same punctuation that opened it, and put a comma before a conjunction that joins two long independent clauses.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: short clauses where modern style omits the comma
- Example: ✗ The server, which runs nightly backs up the database. → ✓ The server, which runs nightly, backs up the database.
